stem_book: The figure shows a system of two blocks connected by a spring, kept on a frictionless surface: a horizontal force F pushes block A (mass m) towards block B (mass 2m), which rests against a vertical wall PQ. Block A is in equilibrium. Suddenly the supporting vertical wall PQ is removed. (a) Initial acceleration of block A is F/m (b) Initial acceleration of block B is F/2m (c) Initial acceleration of block B is zero (d) Initial acceleration of block A is F/3m
key: b Initial acceleration of block B is F/2m
correct_answer: b Initial acceleration of block B is F/2m
work: Spring force = F (equilibrium of A); wall removed: a_A = (F − F)/m = 0, a_B = F/2m
